text:
Once I'd told my husband, things started to move. My GP referred me to a psychologist, who recognised quickly that I was having intrusive thoughts and that they are very common and don't mean anything about who I am. That was a huge relief. We did CBT for the intrusive thoughts, with exposure, which was terrifying at first, for example spending time in the classroom and allowing the thoughts to come without leaving. Over months it became easier.

My husband and I did couples therapy, which helped us reconnect and talk about the infertility honestly. I also started an antidepressant, after discussing it with the fertility clinic.

I wrote to the retreat about what happened. They were kind and apologetic, which I didn't expect, and offered a free integration session, which I declined.

I went back to teaching after five months. I'm doing much better. We're still trying for a baby, and I still have hard days, but I no longer believe what the trip told me.
Ich habe ein paar Stunden Therapie gemacht, das hat bei der Schreckhaftigkeit etwas geholfen. Silvester meide ich weiterhin.

Once my friend named it as trauma, I found a therapist who knew about psychedelic harms. We worked with somatic approaches, to help me feel at home in my body again, and later with EMDR on the images of being torn apart. I also did gradual exposure to dogs, with a friend's very calm old labrador. I distanced myself from the retreat and the community around it, which was hard because many of my friends were part of it. I'm much better now, though I still flinch at large birds.
Mit Freunden darüber geredet, sonst nichts.

I saw a counsellor who explained derealisation and helped me reduce the reality-checking. Keeping a regular sleep schedule helped a lot, and so did avoiding screens before bed so my dreams were less intense.
I talked to a grief counsellor about my grandmother and the guilt. It helped me remember the good times with her, not just that day.

Meine Tochter hat mich zu meinem Hausarzt gebracht, der mich an eine Psychiaterin überwiesen hat. Ich habe ein Antidepressivum bekommen und eine Trauertherapie begonnen. Die Therapeutin hat mir geholfen, die Schuldgefühle zu verstehen und mich von den Bildern aus dem Krankenhaus zu lösen. Ich gehe außerdem in eine Trauergruppe für Witwer, das hat mir sehr geholfen, weil ich gemerkt habe, dass ich nicht allein bin. Ich habe angefangen, ihren Garten weiter zu pflegen, das gibt mir Halt. Die Kisten mit ihren Sachen habe ich inzwischen gemeinsam mit meiner Tochter durchgesehen.
Rested, took a break from mushrooms for a year.

I reached out to a veterans' mental health service, which I'd been avoiding for years. I did a course of trauma-focused therapy with a psychologist who had worked with military medics. We worked on the memory of the private I lost, which I had never talked about. I also joined a veterans' running group. I cut back on drinking. My brother came to one of my therapy sessions, which helped both of us. I'm doing better, but helicopters still get me.
Nichts Besonderes, ging von alleine weg.

I eventually saw a doctor, who examined me and found no injuries, which was reassuring. A psychologist helped me with the panic about lost time and with the derealisation. I took an antidepressant for about a year. Listening to music slowly again, starting with acoustic stuff, helped. I went back to my studies a year later. I still don't know what happened in those 14 hours, and I've had to learn to live with not knowing.

Ich habe einige Sitzungen bei einer Psychotherapeutin gemacht, die mit Atemübungen und Körperwahrnehmung gearbeitet hat. Das hat die Panikattacken deutlich reduziert. Schals trage ich inzwischen wieder.
